主要内容: Best Buy (BBY) reported a 36% increase in sales for the fiscal first quarter of 2022, driven by consumer electronics demand fueled by stimulus spending. The company raised its full-year forecast, citing strong demand continuing into the second quarter. CEO Corie Barry attributed the surge to a strong housing market and government stimulus programs. Best Buy's first-quarter net income rose to $595 million, or $2.32 per share, compared to $159 million, or 61 cents per share, a year earlier. Excluding items, earnings were $2.23 per share, exceeding analyst expectations of $1.39. Revenue reached $11.64 billion, surpassing the $10.44 billion forecast. Online and store sales grew 37.2%, outperforming analyst expectations of 22.4%. The company saw growth across nearly all categories, with the largest gains in home theater, computing, and appliances. Barry noted that new customer growth is 50% higher than pre-pandemic levels, with a shift toward younger, more female, and lower-income shoppers. Best Buy is testing new store formats, including smaller sales floors and experiential locations, as it adapts to changing consumer behavior post-pandemic. The company emphasized the importance of aligning space, location, and other factors to enhance the customer and employee experience. The CEO highlighted the urgency of addressing challenges without compromising the customer and employee experience. As of Thursday's close, Best Buy shares have risen 19% this year, reaching a 52-week high of $128.57 earlier this month. The company's market value stands at $29.58 billion. The CEO also mentioned that the company is not yet in a normalized environment.
